title: Constructible fibre-codimension bounds for a smooth closed pair
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $f:X\to S$ be smooth and of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], where finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $Z\subseteq X$ be a closed subset and let $c\ge0$ be an integer. For $s\in S$ write $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ and $Z_s$ for the inverse image of $Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Put $G_c=\{s\in S:\dim\mathcal O_{X_s,z}\ge c\text{ for every }z\in Z_s\}$, using Krull dimension of local rings [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then $G_c$ is constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset]. For every field extension $K/\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-field-extension], the inequality holds at every point of $Z_s$ if and only if it holds at every point of its inverse image in $X_s\times_{\kappa(s)}K$. Consequently, for every scheme morphism $v:S\prime\to S$, if $X\prime=X\times_SS\prime$, $Z\prime$ is the inverse image of $Z$, and $G_c\prime$ is defined by the same fibrewise local-ring inequalities, then $G_c\prime=v^{-1}(G_c)$. Finally, $s\in G_1$ if and only if $Z_s$ contains no irreducible component of $X_s$ [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Empty fibres and empty $Z_s$ satisfy every bound.

source.place: Tag 05F9 (lemma-dimension-fibres-constructible), applied on the finitely many constant-relative-dimension pieces of a smooth morphism to the closed subset. Field-extension invariance: EGA IV2 Corollary 6.1.4, literature/ega/EGA-IV-2_PMIHES-24-1965.pdf, printed p.136, applied to the surjective flat field-extension projection. This is the constructible-codimension calculation used in EGA IV4 21.14.3(ii).

proof.text: Finite presentation implies finite type: a finite polynomial presentation is a finite set of algebra generators. Thus $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Choose a closed immersion $C\hookrightarrow X$ with image $Z$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme]. By [sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant], the level sets $X_d=\{x:\dim_x X_{f(x)}=d\}$ are clopen. They cover $X$, and quasi-compactness gives only finitely many nonempty levels, indexed by a finite set $D\subset\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Each restriction $X_d\to S$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] (applied to the open cover of $X$ by the $X_d$), and its smooth relative dimension is $d$ by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], since $\dim_x$ of the fibre is computed on any open neighbourhood of $x$ [def-kun-dimension]. Put $C_d=C\times_XX_d$; it is closed in $X_d$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change].

The open $X_d\subseteq X$ and closed $C_d\hookrightarrow X_d$ are of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-closed-finite-presentation], applied with Noetherian ambient scheme $X$. In particular $C_d\to X$ is of finite type, so $C_d$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Quasi-compactness of $C_d$ is also seen directly: $X_d$ is a closed subset of quasi-compact $X$, and $C_d$ is closed in $X_d$; an open cover of a closed subset acquires the open complement to cover the ambient space. The composite $h_d:C_d\to S$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition]. The target $S$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]; $C_d$ is also quasi-separated by that same node. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $h_d$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. It is of finite presentation, exactly as required below.

source.place: Tags 01TR (lemma-composition-finite-presentation), 01OY (lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated), 03GI, 01KV; verification of the hypotheses of 05F9

proof.text: Fix $d\in D$ and $s\in S$, and write $M=(X_d)_s$, $A=(C_d)_s$. The morphisms $X_d\to S$ (composite of the open immersion of [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-closed-finite-presentation] with $f$, locally of finite presentation by [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition], quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) as in step 2) and $h_d$ are of finite presentation, so their base changes $M,A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $k=\kappa(s)$, are of finite presentation, in particular of finite type, by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3); hence $M,A$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; $A$ is closed in $M$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The smooth base-change statement [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] makes $M$ smooth of relative dimension $d$. The closed subset $|A|$ has finitely many irreducible components $W_j$ by [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], with generic points $\eta_j$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. By [lem-kun-dimension-formula] and [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg], $\dim\mathcal O_{M,\eta_j}=d-\dim W_j$. Every $z\in W_j$ is a specialization of $\eta_j$. By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains], a chain of generalizations of $\eta_j$ can be preceded by $z$ if $z\ne\eta_j$, so $\dim\mathcal O_{M,z}\geq\dim\mathcal O_{M,\eta_j}$. Consequently the bound at every $z\in A$ is equivalent to $\dim W_j\leq d-c$ for every $j$.

In the finite union $|A|=\bigcup_jW_j$, each irreducible closed subset lies in some $W_j$: otherwise it is a finite union of proper closed subsets. Hence every chain lies in a component containing its largest member, and $\dim|A|=\max_j\dim W_j$ by the chain definition [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Together with step 3 this gives the exact criterion: if $d\geq c$, the bound on $A$ is equivalent to $\dim|A|\leq d-c$; if $d<c$, it is equivalent to $A=\varnothing$, since every nonempty component has nonnegative dimension. The criterion includes empty $A$, with dimension $-\infty$. These arguments apply to every smooth finite-type $k$-scheme of relative dimension $d$ and every closed subset, independently of the chosen global base.

source.place: Tag 0055 (definition-Krull); elementary finite-closed-union argument and arithmetic from step 3

proof.text: For $h_d$ of step 2, each $E_{d,n}=\{s:\dim|(C_d)_s|=n\}$, $n\geq0$, is constructible by [lem-sfb-finite-presentation-fibre-dimension-levels]. Its nonempty-fibre locus is $h_d(C_d)$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and is constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image]; its empty-fibre locus $N_d=S\setminus h_d(C_d)$ is therefore constructible. Step 4 says that the good locus for piece $d$ is $N_d\cup\bigcup_{n=0}^{d-c}E_{d,n}$ when $d\geq c$, and $N_d$ otherwise. These are finite unions. Since $Z_s$ is partitioned by the finitely many clopen pieces, $G_c$ is their finite intersection. Boolean closure in [def-weil-constructible-subset] proves its constructibility.

source.place: 05F9 (lemma-dimension-fibres-constructible); 054J (lemma-chevalley); 005H Boolean closure; no unbounded union of dimension levels is taken

proof.text: For any finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ and field extension $K/k$, the projection $p:Y_K\to Y$ is surjective by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Apply [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] to $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: $\dim_{y'}Y_K=\dim_{p(y')}Y$ at every point. Taking suprema and using surjectivity gives $\dim|Y_K|=\dim|Y|$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions]. This includes emptiness, since surjectivity shows $Y_K$ is empty exactly when $Y$ is. In particular this applies to $A=(C_d)_s$, without any separatedness hypothesis.

The field extension of $M=(X_d)_s$ is smooth of the same relative dimension $d$ by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], and the inverse image of $A$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Apply the criterion of steps 3--4 to $(M,A)$ and its extension. Step 6 identifies the dimensions of the two closed subsets and detects emptiness, so the criterion is equivalent over $k$ and $K$, on each piece and hence on their union. This proves preservation and reflection of the all-points bound; it does not assert equality of local-ring dimensions at individual lifted points.

source.place: 02NK (lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d), 01QR; applying the explicitly proved criterion in steps 3--4

proof.text: For $s'\in S'$ with $s=v(s')$, [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] identifies $X'_{s'}$ with $X_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(s')$. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies the corresponding closed subset with the inverse image of $Z_s$: both composites to $X$ are the same projection. Apply step 7 with $K=\kappa(s')$. This gives $s'\in G'_c\Longleftrightarrow v(s')\in G_c$, proving $G'_c=v^{-1}(G_c)$ even when $S'$ is not Noetherian.

By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains], $\dim\mathcal O_{X_s,z}=0$ exactly when $z$ has no strict generalization. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober] this says exactly that $z$ is the generic point of an irreducible component: the closure of a generalization contains $\overline{\{z\}}$, and a larger irreducible closed subset has a generic point strictly generalizing $z$. A closed subset $Z_s$ contains such a generic point exactly when it contains its entire component. Thus the bound $c=1$ is precisely absence of an irreducible component in $Z_s$. Empty $Z_s$, including empty fibres, makes every universal inequality vacuous; for $c=0$ nonnegativity of local-ring dimension makes the locus all of $S$.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_closed_fibre_codimension_locus {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [CompactSpace S] (f : X ⟶ S) [Smooth f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] (Z : Set X) (hZ : IsClosed Z) (c : ℕ) : Topology.IsConstructible (f.fibreCodimensionLocus Z c) ∧ (∀ (s : S) (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra (S.residueField s) K], s ∈ f.fibreCodimensionLocus Z c ↔ ∀ z : ↥(pullback (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField s) K)))), f.fiberι s (pullback.fst (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField s) K))) z) ∈ Z → (c : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim ((pullback (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField s) K)))).presheaf.stalk z)) ∧ (∀ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (v : S' ⟶ S), (pullback.snd f v).fibreCodimensionLocus ((pullback.fst f v) ⁻¹' Z) c = v ⁻¹' f.fibreCodimensionLocus Z c) ∧ (∀ s : S, s ∈ f.fibreCodimensionLocus Z 1 ↔ ∀ W ∈ irreducibleComponents (f.fiber s), ¬ W ⊆ (f.fiberι s) ⁻¹' Z) ∧ (∀ s : S, IsEmpty (f.fiber s) → s ∈ f.fibreCodimensionLocus Z c) ∧ (∀ s : S, (f.fiberι s) ⁻¹' Z = ∅ → s ∈ f.fibreCodimensionLocus Z c)
